text: . The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit begins today in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. It is being held to mark the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. The theme of this year’s SCO summit is ‘25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity’. The SCO has 10 member countries, including India, China and Russia. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017.Prime Minister Modi at the Summit venue received a warm welcome. PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping shook hands and interacted while walking together and were seen having a conversation after they posed for a group photograph with other leaders.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The GOBARdhan Central Sector Scheme, with a total outlay of 23,731 crore rupees, has come into effect from today. It marks a major step towards scaling up the production and use of Compressed Biogas in India. The Scheme will be implemented till 2035-36 and will establish Compressed Biogas as a major pillar of India’s future energy mix. The Scheme aims to increase domestic Compressed Biogas, CBG production nearly tenfold, mobilise large-scale private investment and create a vibrant circular bioeconomy across the country. The Union Cabinet had approved the scheme on the 6th of last month.

. Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh,RSS, Sarsangh-chalak Dr Mohan Bhagwat has addressed a large Hindu diaspora gathering in the Greater Toronto Area during his first visit to Canada. The “Hindu Vishwa Bandhu – Embrace the World in Friendship” event was held in Vaughan and attended by more than 2,500 people from eight Canadian provinces. The programme was organized by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue, or CHORD, with support from more than 175 community organizations.Addressing the gathering, Dr Bhagwat highlighted the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the belief that the world is one family. He stressed that diversity in languages, traditions and forms of worship should be respected and seen as a source of unity. Former Canadian Defence Minister and Alberta Premier Jason Kenney attended as chief guest, while Kashmir Singh Dhaliwal of Vancouver’s Khalsa Diwan Society was the guest of honour. The Canada visit is part of Dr Bhagwat’s three-nation outreach to the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom during the RSS centenary year.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended marginally lower today. The Sensex declined 13 points to close at 76,944. The Nifty dropped 25 points to settle at 24,056. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 1.4 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped over 0.2 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened lower amid ongoing geopolitical tensions but recovered from their initial losses and turned positive. However, they failed to sustain their upward momentum during the second half of the session, with the weekly expiry of Nifty Futures and Options contracts adding to the volatility.In the Sensex pack, 17 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top laggards, Maruti declined nearly 4.2 per cent, State Bank of India as well as Indigo dropped around two and a half per cent and Bajaj Finserv lost 2.4 per cent. In contrast, ITC surged four per cent, HCL Tech gained 3.2 per cent and Infosys added over 2.4 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 21 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top underperformers, Auto declined 1.4 per cent, Consumer Durables over 1.2 per cent and Telecommunication as well as Realty dipped over one per cent. In contrast, Information Technology rose over 1.2 per cent, Focused IT gained 1.2 per cent and Energy added over 0.9 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,563 companies declined, 1,760 advanced and 236 remained unchanged.

. The Central Government has revised Special Additional Excise Duty on exports of petrol, diesel and Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) as part of its latest fortnightly review of fuel export taxes. Under the revised rates, the export levy on petrol has been raised to 1.5 rupees per litre, while the duty on diesel has been increased to 25 rupees per litre. The levy on ATF has been trimmed to 19 rupees per litre.The revised rates, notified by the Finance Ministry, came into effect from today. There is, however, no change in the existing excise duty on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption.The Special Additional Excise Duty on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF was introduced with effect from 27th March this year to ensure adequate domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging exports amid the West Asia crisis. The rates are being revised on a fortnightly basis and the last such revision was undertaken with effect from 15th August, 2026. The rates are prescribed based on the average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF prevailing during the period since the last review.

. India and the World Bank Group have discussed expanding their partnership beyond traditional lending, with a sharper focus on infrastructure finance, digital public infrastructure, tourism and the mobilisation of private capital. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met World Bank Group President Ajay Banga on the sidelines of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in Asheville, US.The two leaders discussed a larger role for the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency in India. The proposed engagement would seek to deepen the country’s corporate, infrastructure and municipal bond markets through the systematic use of guarantees and greater mobilisation of private capital. The meeting was focused on ways to strengthen the India-World Bank Group partnership and widen the use of the institution’s financing tools.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has achieved a major milestone in its nationwide mission-mode drive for Mandatory Biometric Updates, completing more than two crore biometric updates for school children across the country. The special drive, initiated in September last year, has now covered over one lakh 56 thousand schools, enabling school children to complete their Aadhaar biometric. Electronics and IT Ministry said that this has helped Mandatory Biometric Updates service to reach children directly at their schools, making the process more accessible and convenient for crores of students.Aadhaar enrolment for children below five years captures demographic information and a photograph, while fingerprints and iris biometrics are not captured at that age as these biometrics are still developing. Mandatory Biometric Updates helps ensure that the child’s Aadhaar continues to have updated biometric information. The Biometric updates are required when a child attains the age of 5 years and again at 15 years. To encourage timely completion and make the service more accessible, UIDAI had waived the charges for  children in the 7 to 15 years age group from 1st October 2025, for a period of one year. The Ministry said that lack of Biometric Updates in Aadhaar may lead to difficulties while carrying out authentication for receiving benefits under various Government schemes, registering in competitive and university examinations.

. The Middle East Energy 2026 event is being held at the Dubai World Trade Centre in UAE from 1st to 3rd September. It is one of the largest international trade exhibitions and conferences for the power and energy industry in the West Asia Region. The event this year is projected to feature over 1900 Exhibitors from over 150 countries, with an estimated 35,000 plus attendees.The India Pavilion at Middle East Energy 2026 features 45 exhibitions by companies from across the country and was inaugurated by India’s Consul General in Dubai, Dr. E. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy.The Indian Exhibitors are showcasing a diverse range of products across the power and energy sector, including transmission and distribution equipment, transformers, cables and electrical systems, renewable-energy and energy-storage solutions, power backup systems, automation and control technologies, and LED lighting. The range highlights India’s broad manufacturing and technology capabilities across the energy value chain.The India pavilion is coordinated and facilitated by the Engineering Export Promotion Council of India (EEPC India), supported by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. The focus has been to provide MSMEs a platform to showcase their products and competence at an international level through participation in such events. UAE is not just an export market for Indian manufacturers but also a potential regional distribution, project-execution and investment hub for the rest of the GCC, West Asia and extending up to Africa.

. In Badminton, India’s leading shuttlers Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma will begin their campaigns today at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Top seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will also be in action in men’s doubles.Earlier, India’s Unnati Hooda made an early exit from the tournament yesterday. World No. 25 Hooda lost to South Korea’s World No. 12 Kim Ga-eun in straight games, 10-21, 18-21, in the opening round of the women’s singles. In Men’s Doubles, the pair of Hariharan Amsakarunan and M R Arjun retired at the first-game interval in their opening-round match. The Indian duo were trailing China’s Chen Bo Yang and Liu Yi, 8-11, when they decided to concede the match.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has renewed his call to embrace Swadeshi goods and avoid unnecessary purchases of gold and destination weddings abroad. In a video message, Prime Minister asked Indians to shun leisure trips abroad, avoid getting married overseas and refrain from buying gold unless necessary. Mr Modi congratulated the country on recording 7.8 percent economic growth and spoke of the need to promote self-reliance and give greater emphasis to swadeshi products.The prime minister said India is progressing rapidly despite global uncertainty, wars, crises and disruptions to supply chains. Taking a swipe at his critics, he said some people within the country, “drowned in an atmosphere of despair”, are spreading the “lies” all around.Mr Modi said the country’s youth will see their dreams being realised through the hard work being put in today. He also called on citizens to continue contributing to the country’s progress, saying the government’s policies and intentions are right.Gold is India’s second-largest import item after oil. Stopping bulk gold purchases dramatically cuts down the country’s collective import bill.

. The International Cricket Council (ICC) has taken away the hosting rights of the inaugural edition of the Women’s Champions Trophy to be held in 2027 from Sri Lanka due to government interference in the administration of Sri Lanka Cricket. According to a report, Sri Lanka was set to host the first-ever edition of the women’s tournament, featuring six teams, including the hosts. But the decision could impact their participation as well. The report added that the ICC is likely to decide on the venue of the tournament in its next board meeting, with the move to strip Sri Lanka from hosting the competition set to make a financial impact on the board. The change of venue is also likely to see the Sri Lanka Women’s team possibly missing out on participating, as the tournament was set to host top five teams along with the host nation.

. India continues to extend all possible assistance to Nepal in the ongoing rescue and relief efforts. The fifth Indian aircraft carrying relief and rescue assistance has departed for Nepal today. In a social media post, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that the aircraft is carrying an 11-member rescue team equipped with specialised equipment, along with 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines.

. The Government has reduced the stock holding limit for sugar dealers from 4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals, effective from the 15th of this month till the 30th of November this year. Our Correspondent reports that the new stock limit is aimed at curbing hoarding and speculative trading, protect consumer interest by ensuring adequate availability and price stability.Currently, a stock holding limit of four thousand quintals on sugar dealers across the country is effective from the 1st of the last month. Under the amended provisions, a sugar dealer shall not hold any stock for a period exceeding 30 days from the date of receipt of such stock.The sugar dealer shall also not keep sugar in stock at any time and in any place throughout the country in excess of two thousand quintals. However, the stock holding limit shall remain at four thousand quintals for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, considering the specific market requirements of the region.The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the Kolkata area is sourcing sugar from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplying it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region.Therefore, the existing limit of four thousand quintals has been retained for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas. The Government has assured consumers that it is taking all necessary steps to maintain adequate availability, orderly supplies and price stability of sugar in the domestic market, while ensuring that genuine trade and distribution activities continue without disruption.

. A 19-member Indian forensic team has begun analysing DNA samples alongside forensic experts to assist in identifying people affected by the recent flash floods in Nepal. The Indian Embassy said that the team commenced the analysis at the Nepal Police Central Forensic Science Laboratory and the National Forensic Science Laboratory in the Khumaltar area of Kathmandu Valley.The Indian experts are working with their counterparts to speed up the processing of DNA samples collected from flood-affected areas and help establish the identities of victims and missing persons. The deployment of Indian forensic team is part of ongoing efforts to support Nepal in the aftermath of the recent flash floods, which caused significant loss of life and left several people unaccounted for.Nepal Police said 1,068 bodies have been recovered by yesterday evening, of which 400 had only partial remains, complicating the identification process. With the death toll continuing to rise following last week’s deadly floods, authorities have collected DNA samples from several unclaimed bodies to support identification efforts in the future.Chitwan district has reported the highest number of recovered bodies so far. Authorities have buried hundreds of bodies in open spaces along riverbanks after collecting DNA samples for future identification. According to Nepal Police, 4,606 people remain unaccounted for, including 583 foreigners, raising concerns that the death toll could increase further. Authorities said efforts are continuing to trace people who remain unaccounted for at various hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will participate in the 18th BRICS Summit later this month in New Delhi. As the chair this year, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The summit will bring together leaders of BRICS member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.The theme for India’s BRICS chairship is ‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability’. India, a founding member of BRICS, has previously held its chairship in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026. BRICS is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.7 percent down at 1,53,183 per 10 grams. Silver fell over 2.8 percent and stood at 2,30,419 rupees per kilogram.

. India and the US have agreed to work more closely on critical minerals following a meeting between Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The agreement aims to strengthen the long-standing economic partnership between the two countries.The two leaders met on the sidelines of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, yesterday. The meeting placed critical minerals and secure supply chains at the centre of the India-US economic dialogue. Both sides acknowledged the long-standing relationship between the two countries and committed themselves to expanding cooperation across several areas.Finance Minister Sitharaman also invited Mr Bessent to visit New Delhi later this year for the India-US Economic and Financial Partnership meeting.The proposed visit will provide the two governments another opportunity to review economic and financial cooperation and identify areas in which the partnership could be expanded.

. India is taking part in the two-day G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) meeting in Asheville, US, on its final day today. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is leading India’s delegation. The meeting, under the US G20 presidency, is focusing on global economic growth, financial stability, rising debt, trade, investment and reforms to the international financial system. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has stressed the need for stronger growth, higher investment and better productivity to tackle growing global debt.India is using the meeting to highlight the needs of emerging economies and promote sustainable growth, trade and investment. New Delhi also wants to strengthen economic ties with G20 countries and present India as a major hub for manufacturing, technology and innovation. The Indian finance ministers held talks with UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey on trade and investment cooperation on the sidelines of the Meet. She also met 3M CEO William Brown to discuss India’s manufacturing, technology and skilled workforce.The meeting also seen disagreements over Russia’s participation on its opening day yesterday. Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended in person, while some European officials skipped the traditional group photograph. Siluanov also met US Treasury Secretary Bessent. China’s large trade surplus is another key issue, with the US pushing for more balanced global trade and greater domestic consumption in China.The US chose Asheville partly to highlight the recovery of western North Carolina after Hurricane Helene. The Main G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to be held in Miami on December 14-15 this year. India’s participation reflects its growing influence in global economic discussions and its efforts to shape policies on trade, investment, growth and financial stability.

. World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka brushed aside Colombia’s Camila Osorio 6-2, 6-4 in the first round of the US Open at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York. Top seed Sabalenka’s second-round clash is against Russia’s Polina Iatcenko as she looks to become only the third woman after Serena Williams and Chris Evert to win three straight US Opens. The Belarusian hit 32 winners against Osorio in a match which lasted an hour and 27 minutes. Osorio handed Sabalenka a break with a ⁠double fault in the third game – one of five she had across the opening set – and slipped 4-1 ‌behind as the Belarusian converted on another break point with an unreturnable backhand.

. Sikkim Shooters performed extraordinarily in 13th North East Zone Shooting Championship 2026. 13th North East Zone Shooting Championship 2026 concluded yesterday at Guwahati, Assam.Laxuman Adhikari from Sikkim won a historic Bronze Medal in the Master Men’s 10m Air Pistol Individual category in this Championship. This was the first-ever medal won by a shooter representing Sikkim at the North East Zonal level.Two shooters from Sikkim Anu Chettri and Tshering Yangden Bhutia have qualified for the 69th National Shooting Championship 2026 after putting up strong performances in 13th North East Zonal Shooting Championship. Chettri secured qualification in the 10m air pistol event, while Bhutia has been selected in 10m air rifle.In total, 11 shooters from Sikkim competed at the Zonal Championship, with the Sikkim Rifle Association contingent comprising eight pistol shooters and three rifle shooters

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at a meeting in New Delhi yesterday. The meeting focused on accelerating implementation of the scheme in the 100 identified districts, strengthening convergence among schemes and improving district-level performance for farmers.The scheme focuses on six key objectives, which are increasing agricultural productivity, promoting crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices, enhancing post-harvest storage capacity, improving irrigation infrastructure, enabling greater access to short- and long-term agricultural credit and improving governance and service delivery.Akashvani correspondent reports that the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare said that the average score of the 100 districts across the six objectives of the scheme increased from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an improvement of 16.31 points. The Ministry said that the scheme is being implemented through the convergence of 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private-sector participation.A total of 121 indicators, comprising 74 output indicators and 47 outcome indicators, have been identified across the 36 schemes for monitoring progress against annual targets.The review emphasised strengthening the monitoring framework to move beyond tracking activities and expenditure towards measuring outcomes and the actual benefits reaching farmers. Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana was approved by the Union Cabinet last year and was launched on 11th October 2025. Shivang Misra, Akashvani News, Delhi.Besides, the Minister also reviewed the progress of the Watershed Development Component (WDC-PMKSY) of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana. During the meeting, Mr Chouhan called upon the States to ensure speedy implementation of projects and clear and measurable outcomes at the grassroots level.He mentioned watershed development as an important tool towards realising the goal of Drought-Free India for Developed India. The minister said watershed development is not just a program to build water bodies, but its real objective is to bring water to the field, increase the productivity of the land, and improve the income of the farmer.

. The External Affairs Ministry has said that 163 Indian nationals have been rescued so far in Nepal with an addition of five more people following flash flood tragedy on 26th of last month. The Ministry informed that the number of Indian nationals rescued yesterday was 158. It added that the number of people who have left China today stands at 151. According to the Ministry, after establishing a foothold at hydropower tunnels in Chilime, the Indian tunnel rescue team had to overcome several challenges such as extremely restricted access space, limitations on use of specialized equipment due to terrain, and a marshy tunnel floor. It added that using innovative methods and improvised floats, the team was able to move deeper in the tunnel. Its efforts will continue tomorrow to try and rescue any individuals that may be trapped inside. Meanwhile, the forensic team from India expanded its activities today in coordination with its counterparts from Nepal, to undertake tasks such as examination of DNA and analysis. This will help expediting the processing of DNA samples in Nepal.

. The Baloch National Movement (BNM) staged a protest in the Netherlands’ Utrecht city, drawing international attention to the ongoing abuses by Pakistani forces in Balochistan, including the enforced disappearance of thousands of people, extrajudicial killings and other serious human rights violations. The demonstration held yesterday to mark the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances brought together several political activists, who expressed solidarity with the victims of enforced disappearances and their families.The International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances is observed every year on August 30, a UN-designated day established in 2011 to raise global awareness of this grave human rights violation and to honour the victims and their families. According to the BNM, the protesters held photographs of forcibly disappeared persons and carried banners and placards while demanding justice and calling for an immediate end to enforced disappearances in Balochistan. Addressing the gathering, the speakers highlighted the profound and devastating impact of enforced disappearances on Baloch society, saying hardly any family in Balochistan has remained untouched by the trauma of enforced disappearance.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with other SCO leaders, participated in the official opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, last evening. The biennial event celebrates the rich sporting traditions, culture and heritage of nomadic civilisations, bringing together countries in a vibrant celebration of their shared culture.Earlier, Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders of Russia, Iran, the Kyrgyz Republic and Armenia on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit. The Prime Minister will address the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit today.

. The Tata Institute of Social Sciences, TISS, conferred degrees on 1,376 students and scholars at its 86th annual convocation held in Mumbai yesterday.The degrees included those awarded to 35 doctoral scholars and graduates from Master’s, Bachelor’s, Integrated and dual-degree programmes.The first undergraduate batch of Analytics and Sustainability Studies also received their degrees. Director of Tata Memorial Hospital, Dr C. S. Pramesh, was the chief guest at the convocation.

. The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal rose to 987 today, with security forces recovering more bodies from eight districts of the country, officials said. Rescuers struggled to trace those stranded amid intermittent rainfall and a fresh flood alert as water levels rose in rivers across several districts. Around 4,000 people, including 583 foreigners and several security personnel, still remain missing, while nearly 12,000 have been rescued, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. Four strengthlifters from Sikkim have been selected to represent India at the upcoming 13th World Strengthlifting and Incline Bench Press (IBP) Championships 2026 in Kyrgyzstan from 8th to 12th September.They are Pema Dorjee Bhutia, Milan Pradhan, Binu Subba and Sangita Tamang. Sikkim Strengthlifting Association (SSA) working president Alan Targen congratulated the selected athletes and wished them success in the upcoming championship.Pema Dorjee Bhutia expressed confidence in their ability to perform well at the upcoming championship. Bhutia said the selection was not only a personal achievement for the athletes but also a proud moment for Sikkim and the state’s strengthlifting fraternity

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. In Men’s Cricket, India’s 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan has been announced.Shreyas Iyer will lead the Indian side, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. Ace seamer Jasprit Bumrah returns to the squad, subject to fitness clearance, along with Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana. Bumrah missed India’s recent assignments after suffering a knee injury during the ODI series in England in July. He also missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka.The series will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on the 13th, 15th and 17th of this month. Afghanistan will be the designated host for the series.The Indian top order features a mix of experienced campaigners and young talent, including Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan.The middle order features the likes of skipper Shreyas Iyer, vice-captain Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube. India have opted for three all-round options in Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, while Varun Chakaravarthy will lead the spin attack alongside Ravi Bishnoi.The pace attack will be spearheaded by Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh, with Harshit Rana providing an additional option with his effective cutters.The squad largely mirrors India’s team for the upcoming Asian Games to being at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan from 19th of this month.

. Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 20-year Argentina career that included a World Cup triumph, two Copa América titles and a record 207 appearances for his country. Messi said the decision had been on his mind since the World Cup final defeat to Spain, before the death of his father further convinced him it was time to step away. The 39-year-old revealed the decision in a statement posted on his official Instagram account, confirming that he would no longer wear the Argentina jersey after one of the most celebrated international careers in football history.Messi said the decision had been painful, particularly because of the emotional bond he has shared with the national team and Argentina’s supporters throughout his career. He led his country to the World Cup title in 2022 after years of near misses and also helped Argentina win two Copa América crowns. His international journey also included World Cup final defeats in 2014 and again this summer, with the loss to Spain in July proving to be a significant moment in his decision-making process.

. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has shared details regarding the identification and repatriation of mortal remains of victims of the recent flash floods in Nepal. The Embassy said that, as per the Government of Nepal, several steps are required for handing over the mortal remains of foreign nationals.These include documentation of the mortal remains, recording photographs and details, post-mortem examination, verification of the cause of death, formal identification, collection of fingerprints, DNA and other forensic samples, verification of the deceased person’s passport or identity document, and completion of Embassy or consular coordination.The Embassy said that if relatives and family members are able to identify the mortal remains through photographs and descriptions available on the Nepal Police website, it will assist in coordinating with local authorities for the handover and repatriation of the mortal remains. It added that the Government of Nepal has carried out temporary interment of a large number of mortal remains to prevent health risks. The identification of such remains would require DNA matching with first-degree relatives.In cases where identification is not possible or the mortal remains have been temporarily interred, the Government will facilitate DNA matching. The Embassy said that people requiring assistance can contact the Embassy on the helpline at +977 985 131 6807, +977 970 910 7500, and +977 981 032 6117.

India has shown that it can adjust to changes in the global economy without allowing its growth to be derailed, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman has said while acknowledging the country’s dependence on imported energy and fertilisers. Finance Minister Sitharaman described India as a vibrant and responsive economy capable of managing external challenges, reports said today.India is among the world’s large importers of crude oil and petroleum products. It also imports several fertilisers and their inputs despite having some domestic production capacity, the Finance Minister said. Sitharaman highlighted India’s economic performance, which demonstrated its ability to respond to developments overseas and protect its growth momentum.The Finance Minister said the Reserve Bank of India also periodically issues its assessment of the economy, with the indicators moving in a positive direction. Sitharaman also highlighted India’s recorded growth of 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the 2026-27 financial year. India’s foreign exchange reserves stood at about USD 700 billion, according to the Finance Minister. As per the report, Sitharaman credited Indian citizens, economic reforms and the expansion of digital infrastructure for strengthening the economy.Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has also said that India is preparing further customs and banking reforms, including risk-based import screening and a high-level review of the banking sector’s role towards building a developed India.The Finance Minister said the next phase would build on changes already made in direct and indirect taxation, reports said today. Sitharaman also stated that the government is working to make the movement of imported goods through Indian ports more seamless. In this regard, a key proposal involves deploying scanners and concentrating checks on high-risk importers. Other consignments could then be cleared automatically, reducing delays for businesses and easing congestion at ports.The approach would allow customs authorities to focus their scrutiny on higher-risk imports while facilitating faster clearances in other cases. However, FM Sitharaman did not provide a timetable for introducing the scanners or implementing the proposed automatic clearance system.Sitharaman said confidence in the Indian banking system was reflected in foreign deposits and investments made by Indians living overseas. The indicators showed a positive story about trust in Indian banks and the country’s macroeconomic position, she said.

The Government said that the country has adequate availability of onion and it has begun a calibrated and targeted release of buffer stocks through Kanda Express and road transport to ensure moderation of seasonal price pressures. The Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Ministry said that retail intervention efforts have expanded significantly across 19 cities, supported by the dispatch of over 30 trucks to ensure widespread availability.The Ministry has informed that two Kanda Express consignments have been dispatched from Nashik as part of this initiative. It added that the first rake, carrying 450 Metric Tonnes of onions, reached Delhi and was subsequently distributed across Varanasi, Lucknow, Chandigarh and Amritsar and across the Delhi-NCR region. The Ministry further said that the second rake, carrying 840 MT of onions, reached Chennai yesterday and is likely to be distributed across various districts of Tamil Nadu. The Ministry noted that around one thousand Metric Tonnes of onions are being transported by road to major consumption centres, based on prevailing market conditions and price trends.The Ministry has informed 210 crore rupees have been paid directly to around three thousand 400 farmers, ensuring timely payments. The Government remains committed to supporting onion farmers while ensuring adequate and affordable availability for consumers. The Government has also put in place robust security measures to prevent any leakages and address security concerns during the movement and disposal of large quantities of onions through railway rakes.It highlighted that the release of onions from buffer stocks has improved market availability and prices have shown a decline from the day following the commencement of disposal, with increased supplies expected to further support price stability.

. The US has begun fresh strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets inside Iran. Iranian media reported that explosions were heard in Bandar Abbas, Hormuz, Asaluyeh, Jiroft, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Chabahar, Jask, Sirik and Lavan.US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it completed the wave of strikes against Iranian military targets, which included air defence sites, mine-laying capabilities, and communications sites, among others. It said that the strikes follow recent attempted attacks by IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said that the US strikes hit a home hosting a wedding ceremony in the city of Kuhestak, resulting in the deaths of four civilians and over 50 injuries.US President Donald Trump, in a post on Truth Social, has warned that any retaliation by Iran against the very justified attack will see a stronger response by Washington. Trump also hinted that a much bigger attack against Tehran is yet to come.In response, Iran’s IRGC claimed an attack on US military barracks at Jordan’s Camp Titin. Iran’s army said it targeted US forces stationed at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa airbase. Kuwait’s army said the country’s air defences responded to attacks by “hostile drones” from Iran.

. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit of the Jal Shakti Ministry in New Delhi today. The summit is bringing together the Centre and States to deliberate on critical sectoral priorities and evolve time-bound action plans.The summit is focusing on four key areas covering timely implementation of Water Infrastructure Projects, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari – Catch the Rain, Drinking Water Source Sustainability and Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
